sub_scenario.one_line: site reliability engineer: poor fit under the current charter

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the evidence table and closing stale entries.
The alert review review wrapped early today.
Ambiguity itself does not scare me; slow-burning mystery tickets are my favorite work.
Time and a place to write.
Someone new shadowed me in the reliability channel this morning.
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the incident causes into one message before lunch.
During the database stall I wrote a three-column table of observed, inferred, and unknown before the owner call, and we picked the right subsystem on the first try.
It kept my guesses out of my facts.
I have owned plenty of clear-cut escalations verbally with zero drama.
When evidence is unambiguous, verbal is fine?
I archived last cycle's notes on the alert review and set up the new folder.
As fresh as these things get.
Give me a scribe or a shared doc during an incident and my accuracy jumps; I have watched it happen for two years.
A vendor call about the evidence table ran long but ended well.
I walked through the reliability channel checklist with the new starter.
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the incident causes.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the alert review records and fixed it at the source.
On the paging bridge in May I was pushed to name a probable cause inside five minutes; I said connection pool, we rolled back the wrong service, and the real fault sat untouched for an hour.
Logs landed twenty minutes after my guess did the damage.
I sketched next week's plan for the incident causes before leaving.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the evidence table updates.
The rapid-response pod's charter explicitly times the first cause statement at five minutes; I asked whether a written-first variant was possible and the answer was no.
I compared two options for the alert review tooling and noted a mild preference.
I closed the week by updating the reliability channel handover notes.
The team lead asked me straight: is the rapid-response pod, as it currently operates, a place where my incident work would be at its best?
